text:
emma: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on prod after yesterday's FP8 calibration update for Mistral-8B and Qwen-7B profiles. p50 token latency up ~18-22% on 512-length tails. Logs attached below.

raj: Ack. Which change exactly? the new per-layer scale clipping or the global clip? :thinking:

emma: It was the per-layer asymmetric clipping by default + slight change in kernel selection order (prefer fp8-kernel-v2). Repro locally on a dev pool after switching to the new profile.

marco: Can you paste the profiler output? also which batch sizes saw the regressions?

emma: Profiler snippet:
```
[PROFILE] model=mistral-8b quant=fp8 per_layer_clip=true kernel_order=[fp8-v2,int8-v1,4bit-v1]
[SUM] p50=38.2ms p95=120.4ms throughput=88 tok/s
[BASE] older-profile (fp8-v1): p50=32.4ms p95=106.1ms throughput=104 tok/s
[KV] KV cache hit ratio ~0.85 during warmup, but cold starts spike latency a lot
[BATCH] avg_batch=4 window=12ms -> batching dropped to single-token paths often
```

sophia: Interesting — looks like kernel selection is choosing fp8-v2 even when sequence length is small causing different memory access pattern? fp8-v2 has a fused gemm path that benefits long sequences but has worse per-call overhead.

liam: Also saw KV cache thrashing on newer kernels. The fp8-v2 path currently re-allocs a small temporary buffer per layer with different alignment which might invalidate some cache prefetch assumptions.

raj: Two potential levers: 1) make kernel selection cost-model aware of per-request sequence length + batch size, 2) warmup KV cache paths earlier (run a cheap prefix through new kernel once per worker).

emma: Agreed. Quick experiment: forcing kernel_order to [int8-v1, fp8-v2] restores previous p50 almost exactly. But int8 sometimes degrades output quality; need a hybrid rule: prefer int8 for requests <256 tokens or batch_size<=2, use fp8 for bigger.

marco: Can we share model-specific quant profiles in repo so teams don't re-create slightly different calibration datasets? I think mismatched calibration between Mistral and Qwen is causing different kernel performance characteristics.

sophia: Yes — proposal: a profiles/ dir with YAML like `mistral-8b-fp8.yaml` and `qwen-7b-fp8.yaml` containing calibration seeds, clip strategy, and kernel hints. Also include a quick perf matrix for common seq lengths.

liam: I'll prototype a selection heuristic patch that checks: if seq_len<256 -> prefer int8-kernel; if batch_size<=2 -> prefer int8; else if seq_len>=512 -> fp8. Also add an opt-in field in profile to pin kernels.

emma: One more thing — batching heuristics: the runtime currently uses a fixed 12ms batching window. For mixed workloads (chattier short requests + long completions) we should adapt the window based on recent request length distribution. Short-term suggestion: dynamic window that shrinks if >70% of last 100 requests are <=8 tokens.

raj: Good. Can we log a compact feature vector for each request to the perf trace so we can replay selection decisions? e.g., `features:seq_len,batch_size,kv_hit,profile_id` — perf-bot could aggregate.

perf-bot: New trace tag created: quant_profile_experiment_v2. Aggregation scheduled for 6h.

marco: For calibration effects on quality: let's add a standard eval set (100 prompts, multifaceted) and run automatic delta checks when changing clip strategy. If quality drop >0.5% on rouge/acc, fail the profile change.

sophia: Also want to record per-layer scale distributions in the calibration artifacts. We might be missing heavy-tailed layers for Qwen that make fp8-v2 unstable.

liam: I'll open a PR with: (A) selection heuristic patch, (B) profiles/ dir with two example files, (C) an opt-in kernel_pin flag. Will add perf numbers in the PR description.

emma: Awesome. Action items: liam PR, marco to add eval set + CI check, raj to add perf logging vector, sophia to collect per-layer scale hist for Qwen and Mistral. I'll roll back default to fp8-v1 for now to reduce customer impact. :lock:

marco: noted. thanks. :thumbsup:

emma: TL;DR — regression traced to fp8-v2 + per-layer clip defaults; short-term revert, medium-term smarter kernel selection + shared model profiles + eval gating.
